absent: Locking, concurrency and ordering rules for all interfaces in these fragments.
Error codes, validation failures and permission checks for the control requests.
Kernel-side state transitions, lifetime ownership and cleanup behavior.
Byte order, packing and cross-architecture alignment beyond the declared field widths.
Semantics of flags fields whose values are not enumerated in the fragments.

findings.text: EEH partition error detail holds a type selector and function selector as narrow words followed by wide address and mask words. The operation envelope starts with size, flags and operation selector words and then offers a variant area that currently carries only the error detail record.

Partition operations use small integers where disable is zero and enable is one, IO unfreeze is two and DMA unfreeze is three, state retrieval is four, reset deactivation is five, hot reset is six, fundamental reset is seven, configure is eight and error injection is nine. Reported states use zero for normal, one for reset in progress, two for fully stopped, four for DMA-only stopped and five for unavailable. The control request is encoded at VFIO base plus 21.

The partition is observed in one of normal, resetting, fully stopped, DMA-stopped or unavailable conditions. Management requests move it between enabled and disabled behavior, release IO or DMA after freezing, query the current condition, assert or release reset flavors, apply configuration, or inject an error for testing.

SPAPR memory registration carries size and flags plus a process virtual address and byte length. Table creation carries size and flags, page shift with a reserved word, window size, level count with a second reserved word, and returns a start address. Table removal carries size and flags plus the start address to destroy.
SPAPR container controls are four sequential requests at VFIO base offsets 17 through 20 for register, unregister, table create and table remove respectively.
Device dump note header contains name length, content length and note type words, then a fixed eight byte owner field and a fixed device-name area whose capacity is defined by a separate maximum.

Dump notes use owner name LINUX and allow up to 44 bytes for the device dump name. Recoverable hardware error categories are ordered CPU, memory, PCI, CXL and others, terminated by a maximum sentinel.

Virtual terminal mode holds a mode byte and wait flag plus release, acquire and spare signal selectors. Global state holds active console, signal to send and console bitmask. Size variants hold rows, columns and scrollback, or add pixel geometry per screen and per character. Events hold an event code plus old and new console identities with padding for growth. Combined activate holds a console number with an embedded mode. Console size plus cursor position holds console rows and columns with cursor row and column.

Consoles range from a minimum of one to a maximum of 63, with serial lines starting at 64. Switching modes use zero for automatic, one for process controlled and two for acknowledged acquisition. Event bits use one for switch, two for blank, four for unblank and eight for resize, with F as the combined maximum.

Console management exposes sequential requests from 0x5600 for open query through 0x560F for combined activate and mode setting, covering get and set mode, get state, send signal, release display, activate, wait active, disallocate, two resize forms, switch lock and unlock, high font mask query and event wait. An additional read request retrieves console size with cursor position.

Wait option bits use one for no-hang, two for untraced with stopped as an alias, four for exited and eight for continued. Poll without reaping uses bit 24. High selectors use bit 29 to exclude other threads, bit 30 for all children and bit 31 for non-SIGCHLD children. Identifier types use zero for all, one for pid, two for group and three for pidfd.

Watch header packs a 24 bit notification type with an 8 bit subtype, followed by an info word partitioned into length, watchpoint identifier and type-specific info with flag aliases. A per-type filter holds type, info value and mask plus an eight word subtype bitmask. The filter envelope holds a count and reserved word plus a trailing variable array. Removal extends the header with a wide type-dependent identifier. Key delivery extends the header with affected key identifier and auxiliary data.

Notification pipes are selected by aliasing the pipe creation flag to exclusive mode. Queue sizing and filter installation use W-series requests 0x60 and 0x61. Top-level types are zero for metadata and one for key notification with two as count. Metadata subtypes are zero for removal and one for loss. Info encoding reserves low seven bits for length at shift zero, next byte for identifier at shift eight and high half for type info at shift sixteen, with eight flag aliases occupying the high-half bits. Key subtypes run zero through seven from instantiation, update, link, unlink, clear, revoke and invalidate to attribute change.
Extended attribute arguments carry an aligned wide value carrier together with size and flags words.

Attribute creation uses one to fail when present and replacement uses two to fail when absent. Namespace prefixes include os2, osx, btrfs, gnu, security, system, trusted and user forms, each with a length defined as storage size minus terminator. Security namespaces compose names for EVM, IMA, SELinux, several SMACK variants including network, execution, transmute and mapping forms, AppArmor, capabilities and BPF LSM, while system namespaces compose access and default POSIX ACL names.

Transform address storage overlays a single IPv4 word, four IPv6 words and a native IPv6 address. Association identity pairs destination address with SPI and protocol. Security context pairs domain and algorithm selectors with length, session identifier and counted trailing string. Selector combines destination and source addresses, port values with masks, family, prefix lengths, protocol, interface index and user identity. Lifetime configuration holds soft and hard byte, packet, add-expiry and use-expiry limits, while current lifetime holds bytes, packets and add and use times. Replay state holds output and input sequence numbers with bitmap, with an extended form adding high sequence parts, window and variable bitmap. Algorithm descriptors share a fixed 64 byte name with key length in bits and trailing key material, adding truncation length for authentication or ICV length for AEAD. Statistics hold replay window, replay count and integrity failure count.

Security domains use zero for reserved and one for LSM, with algorithms zero reserved and one SELinux. Policy categories use zero main, one sub, two maximum and 255 any. Directions use zero in, one out, two forward, three as mask and maximum. Association directions use one in and two out. Sharing ranges from any through session and user to unique use. Modes run zero transport, one tunnel, two route optimization, three in-trigger, four BEET, five IPTFS and six maximum. Infinite lifetime is all-ones and extended replay bitmap capacity is 4096.

Transform netlink management forms a consecutive family starting at base 16 covering association, policy, SPI allocation, acquire, expiry, update, flush, audit events, report, migrate, SAD and SPD info, mapping and default operations through migrate state, with maximum and type-count values derived arithmetically from the endpoints.

User security context header holds length, extension type, algorithm, domain and context length. Template entry holds association identity, family, source address, request identifier, mode, sharing, optional flag and three algorithm masks for authentication, encryption and compression. Encapsulation template holds type, source and destination ports and original address. Policy type qualifier holds a type byte with reserved padding.

Asynchronous event flags use zero for unspecified, with distinct bits for replay threshold, replay value, lifetime value, expiry threshold and cause indications for replay update, timer expiry and policy update, plus a derived maximum.

Reserved and padding fields preserve extensibility and alignment: SPAPR creation reserves two words, filter and policy qualifiers reserve words that must stay zero, terminal spare signal and event padding are zero, and fixed buffers have exact capacities for algorithm names, subtype masks, dump names and note owners.

Several structures end in caller-sized data whose length lives in another field, so truncation and overrun checks matter: envelope size fields, counted security strings, filter arrays, replay bitmaps, algorithm keys, and bit-packed notification info where length, identifier and flags share one word.

These headers export userspace-visible device, console, notification, attribute and transform contracts through stable structures, numeric operation codes and control requests rather than kernel-internal helpers.
